extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, scholarly-society staff, and scholarly-communications professionals interested in diversity, equity, and inclusion in peer review and authorship
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and findings about measuring and responding to demographic patterns in co-authorship, reviewer selection, and submissions to identify and reduce bias in peer review and related scholarly activities. Focuses on what metadata to collect, what patterns to look for, and institutional actions to promote equitable networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect self-reported demographic metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect gender (self-reported), birth year (age), national affiliation, and for U.S. participants race/ethnicity (using a simple set based on the U.S. Census).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having age data is critical to distinguish age-related differences from bias; collecting self-reported gender avoids the uncertainty of name-gender algorithms. Use consistent category sets (e.g., Census-derived) and link membership/journal/meeting datasets to maximize matching. Empty if none: ''

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying on name-gender algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: Name-based gender inference has uncertainty close to the potential effect of bias in many cases and should be avoided when self-reported data are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, use self-reported gender rather than inferred gender. The interview cites Elsevier and other studies that worked around both data and inference issues. Empty if none: ''

rubrics_metrics.name: Include age (birth year) when analyzing representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include age data to identify whether apparent gender or minority imbalances are due to age-distribution differences (e.g., younger cohorts being more female).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age lets you ask whether reviewers or invited speakers are just older (and thus predominantly male) or whether there is true gender bias. Omitting age risks conflating cohort effects with bias. Empty if none: ''

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure homophily in co-authorship networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether authors interact more with people of the same gender or age group than expected (homophily).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AGU data show women interact more with women and men with men across ages and that both genders have more co-authors within their own age group than expected. Use network analysis of co-author pairs (AGU had >400,000 unique co-author pairs) to quantify homophily. Empty if none: ''

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess international collaboration patterns by gender
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare international co-authorship rates between men and women and across countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU found men in most countries have more international co-authors than women; these differences vary by country. Analyze geographic affiliation alongside gender and age to detect disparities. Empty if none: ''

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze impact of team diversity on outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether team diversity (gender, age, possibly race/ethnicity) correlates with measures of success such as acceptance rates and citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU found diverse gender and age teams improve citations and acceptance rates (stronger effect for male first authors in AGU journals); evidence for racial/ethnic diversity effects was inconclusive due to smaller sample size. Use journal manuscripts for quality/outcome analysis, and abstracts/meeting data for network structure. Empty if none: ''

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor submission and acceptance rates by demographic groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Track submissions and acceptance rates broken down by gender, age, nationality, and race/ethnicity over time (including during shocks such as the COVID-19 pandemic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU monitors submission and acceptance patterns and notes no significant gender difference in submissions so far during COVID-19, though geography shifted slightly. Ongoing monitoring is important to detect changes and inform policy. Empty if none: ''

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and address convener/organizer network bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that session conveners and organizers often include their own co-authors in sessions/submissions (AGU found ~35% involve co-authors of conveners), which can reinforce network-based bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Societies and meeting organizers should design processes to reduce automatic inclusion of conveners' co-authors (e.g., conflict-of-interest rules, broader solicitation practices) to avoid reinforcing inequitable networks. Empty if none: ''

rubrics_metrics.name: Use large, linked datasets for statistical power
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine membership, meeting, and journal datasets to gain large sample sizes (e.g., hundreds of thousands of co-author pairs) for reliable statistical inference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU's advantage is the ability to link member-provided demographics across journals and meetings; this scale provides strong statistical significance for network and outcome analyses. Empty if none: ''

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicly report DE&I metrics and use dashboards
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations should publicly measure and report diversity, equity, and inclusion metrics (e.g., honors/awards diversity) and create organization-wide D&I dashboards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU is proactively measuring and publicly reporting DE&I and gender diversity results in honors and awards and plans an organizational dashboard. Public reporting supports accountability and monitoring over time. Empty if none: ''

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement proactive institutional and funder policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders, societies, departments, advisors, and institutions should actively require or incentivize efforts to expand equitable professional networks and include diverse perspectives in proposals and projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The interview suggests funders could ask about or require network-expansion and diversity efforts in proposals, especially for large projects. Mentorship and institutional policies should support young scientists in developing broad networks. Empty if none: ''

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote inclusive scientific culture across identities
rubrics_metrics.description: DE&I policies and practices should address not only gender and race but also ableness, status, gender identity, sexual orientation, and other identities where bias can manifest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU's strategic plan explicitly lists promoting an inclusive scientific culture as a high-level goal; analyses and policies should consider multiple identity axes. Empty if none: ''

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious interpreting small-sample subgroup results
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize when sample sizes for certain demographic subgroups (e.g., racial/ethnic minorities) are small, limiting statistical significance of findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU noted that for teams including racial/ethnic minorities the sample size was smaller and thus conclusions about outcomes (citations/acceptance) had low statistical significance. Use appropriate caveats and seek larger or pooled datasets where possible. Empty if none: ''

rubrics_metrics.name: Use co-authorship as a measurable proxy for professional networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat authorship teams as measurable approximations of professional/social networks that influence reviewer selection, invited speakers, and opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because authors and editors often suggest reviewers or invite people from their networks, analyzing co-authorship reveals how networks form early and reinforce bias; use this proxy to inform interventions. Empty if none: ''
